B.source: Sorry, I need to leave early today.

notes: Work/social. Statement, not a request; politeness marker is the apology 'sorry'. Default: plain statement or a permission question ('Can I leave early?'), a speech-act change.

A.source: Please wait until I finish typing my answer.

B.source: Wait until I finish typing my answer.

notes: AAC conversation pace (adult self-advocacy). Agent = addressee (wait). Default: polite.

A.source: Print a copy of the contract.

B.source: Could you print a copy of the contract?

notes: Work. Default: polite.

A.source: Please book me a taxi for the airport.

B.source: Book me a taxi for the airport.

notes: Travel. Default: polite.

A.source: Feed the cat while I'm away.

B.source: Would you feed the cat while I'm away?

notes: Pets/neighbours. Agent of 'feed' = addressee. Default: polite.

A.source: Please bring a dish to the potluck.

B.source: Bring a dish to the potluck.

notes: Social/community. Default: polite.

context: In a shop, after a billing mistake.

A.source: Speak to the store manager for me.

B.source: Could you speak to the store manager for me?

notes: Self-advocacy/shopping. Default: polite, or speaker ('I want to speak to the manager'), an agent change.

A.source: Please put the shopping in the boot.

B.source: Put the shopping in the boot.

notes: Shopping/transport. Default: polite.

A.source: Move your car from the driveway.

B.source: Would you mind moving your car from the driveway?

notes: Neighbours. 'mind' is part of the softener. Default: polite.

A.source: Please show me how the banking app works.

B.source: Show me how the banking app works.

notes: Tech/money. Default: polite.

A.source: Read the menu out loud to me.

B.source: Could you read the menu out loud to me?

notes: Vision/access, restaurants. Default: polite.

A.source: Please check the train times for Saturday.

B.source: Check the train times for Saturday.

notes: Travel. Default: polite.

A.source: Return the drill this week.

B.source: Could you return the drill this week?

notes: Neighbours/DIY. Default: polite.

A.source: Please explain the phone bill to me.

B.source: Explain the phone bill to me.

notes: Money/admin. Default: polite.

A.source: Lend me your charger for the night.

B.source: Would you lend me your charger for the night?

notes: Tech/travel. Default: polite.

A.source: Can you keep an eye on my bag for a minute?

B.source: Could you keep an eye on my bag for a minute?

notes: CB-2: 'Can you' is plain, 'Could you' polite; the pair differs in one modal. Default: polite or 'Can you'.

A.source: Will you tidy the kitchen tonight?

B.source: Would you tidy the kitchen tonight?

notes: 'Will you' (plain, not in the polite list) vs 'Would you' (polite). Both requests. Default: polite or 'Can you'.

A.source: Pass me the bread knife, thanks.

B.source: Pass me the bread knife.

notes: Polite without please: 'thanks' on an imperative (as pol2-05). Default: 'please' (a different polite marker still matches 'polite').

A.source: Sorry, I didn't catch your full name.

B.source: I didn't catch your full name.

notes: Polite without please, and not a request: apology on a statement. Negation shared (in all_chips). Default: a question/request ('What's your name?'), a speech-act change.

A.source: Ask Jo to please call me back this afternoon.

B.source: Ask Jo to call me back this afternoon.

notes: 'please' inside an embedded (relayed) request. No agent chip: addressee (ask) vs Jo (call) is contestable. Default: polite, probably sentence-initial 'Please ask Jo...'.

A.source: Can I pay by card here, please?

B.source: Can I pay by card here?

notes: Permission question, not a request: 'Can I ..., please?' = question with please (CB-9); B plain (CB-2). Default: polite.

A.source: Where is the lift in this building?

B.source: Sorry, where is the lift in this building?

notes: Polite without please on an information question (apology opener). No agent chip (locative copula). Default: plain question or 'Could you tell me...' (polite).

A.source: Leave the parcel by the back door, thanks.

B.source: Leave the parcel by the back door.

notes: Polite without please: closing 'thanks' on an instruction to a courier. Default: polite.

A.source: Can you spell the street name?

B.source: Sorry, can you spell the street name?

notes: Polite only through 'sorry'; 'Can you' alone is plain (CB-2) in both. Default: polite or 'Can you'.

A.source: Sam, please wash the roasting pans.

B.source: Sam, wash the roasting pans.

notes: Vocative before the imperative; 'please' after the vocative, not sentence-initial. Default: polite.
